name: LexIQ
description: A word game for MiniPay. You get seven letters and a countdown, and build as many words as you can before the clock runs out. Playable as a guest with no wallet; signing in adds daily and weekly leaderboards. English, French and Spanish.

questions.text: You have never seen this before. Within ten seconds of the page loading, how clear is it what this is and what you are meant to do? 1 = no idea, 10 = completely obvious.
What was the single most confusing thing on first load, and what would have removed that confusion? Be specific about what you saw on screen.
Without being told, can you work out how a word scores and why one word is worth more than another? Say what you worked out and what stayed unclear.
Judging it as a phone-first app at roughly 360x640, how usable is the layout? 1 = unusable, 10 = designed for this. Mention anything cut off, overlapping, or too small to tap.
Did anything behave as though it were broken, stuck, mislabelled, or contradictory? Describe what you did, what you expected, and what actually happened.
Is it clear you can play without signing in, and what signing in actually gets you? Quote the wording that told you, or say why it was unclear.
If this arrived in a wallet app you already use, how likely would you be to open it a second time the next day? 1 = never, 10 = certainly. Say what would raise that number.
